debit.rmn: Call our customer care number 0497 2717800 from the registered mobile number and follow the IVR instructions.
debit.sms: Send SMS to 9230600500 in the format HOTLIST + last four digits of the ATM Card Number (page example: HOTLIST 1234).
debit.notes: Lost-card FAQ on the RuPay debit-card page: 'Immediately Hotlist / Block your Debit Card by calling 0497 2717800'; SMS self-service HOTLIST + last four digits of the ATM card number to 9230600500; IVR hotlist by calling customer care 0497 2717800 from the registered mobile number; mobile-banking users block inside the app ('KGB mPAY application ... Click on ATM card Menu >> click Temporary Block/Unblock >> Use toggle button to block debit card usage'); or inform the branch to hotlist the card. The site header publishes Toll Free Number 1800 425 4000 (this number is also the published WhatsApp banking number, 1800-425-4000) and Customer Care Number 0497-2717800; no service hours are published for either line and no overseas number is published. KGBNet internet banking (netbanking.kgb.bank.in) offers 'hot-listing of Debit Card' under its online Request Services — 'Debit card can be hot-listed online. User will receive the status over SMS to the registered Mobile Number' — and is advertised as 24 X 7 banking; the KGB INFI mobile app is advertised as 24/7. The site's published app-store links point to KGB INFI as the bank's mobile banking app ('Available for both Android and iOS users'), while the blocking FAQ still names the older KGB mPAY app; no store link labelled mPAY is published. Customer-care email is published in the contact page's structured data as customercare.kgb@kgb.bank.in (also shown obfuscated as customercare[dot]kgb[at]kgb[dot]bank[dot]in); the complaints portal is connect.kgb.bank.in. No mention of the 1930 cyber helpline appears on the bank's checked pages.

credit.notes: No credit-card product or credit-card blocking channel is published: the site's Cards menu lists only RuPay Debit Cards, Junior Debit Card and Kisan Credit Card (a farm-loan card), /personal-banking/credit-cards and /personal-banking/credit-card returned 404 in the same live check, and the only 'credit card' wording on the debit page is generic CVV-copy. The earlier entry's credit-card channels (toll-free 1800-425-1829, customercare@keralagbank.in) appear nowhere on the current official site; the bank's published care lines under 'debit' are its card-blocking channels.

upi.notes: No UPI block/freeze channel of any kind is published on the bank's official pages fetched live on 2026-11-01: the UPI Services page (kgb.bank.in/services/upi) documents registration through third-party UPI apps only — 'Kerala Grameena Bank has been onboarded to Unified Payment Interface (UPI) platform'; 'Download any of the UPI apps like BHIM, Google Tez, etc'; 'Create a Virtual Payment Address (VPA / UPI ID)'; 'Set MPIN' — with no lock/freeze/deregister step, and the KGB INFI app-store listings the site links (developer Kerala Gramin Bank) publish no UPI block/freeze or manage feature (Play 'Key Features': 'Fund Transfer to other Bank Accounts using NEFT, RTGS and IMPS', 'ATM, POS and eCOM transaction limit setting', 'Facility to deactivate and reactivate Mobile Banking'; the App Store description field has zero UPI mentions — only NEFT/IMPS transfers and 'Enhanced Debit Card Control – Set limits, enable/disable transactions'; the only UPI wording anywhere on the App Store page is release-history text, '2. UPI Help & Support' in the v1.0.62 release note dated Sun Jan 04 2026 — a support entry, not a freeze path), so no in-app UPI lock can be verified; no netbanking UPI manage/disable option is published (KGBNet internet banking at netbanking.kgb.bank.in publishes online Request Services for 'hot-listing of Debit Card' only); and no SMS keyword or *99# usage for UPI appears on any fetched page. The closest published action is facility-level policy prose, not a UPI path: the Mobile Banking Policy (2024-25) says on a changed or no-longer-used mobile number the 'customer shall take immediate action to deregister from KGBmPAY', 'If the Mobile Phone Number or SIM is lost, the user must immediately take action to deregister from the facility', and 'If the customer suspect the misuse of the MPIN, customer should immediately initiate necessary steps to change the MPIN'. Phone fallback for UPI issues: the UPI Services page itself publishes 'Customer Support 0497 2717800 / 1800 425 4000' and displays 'Toll Free Number 1800 425 4000'; the published complaints portal connect.kgb.bank.in ('Public Grievances Redressal System') is OTP-gated, so whether it offers a UPI complaint category is not verifiable without OTP; no mention of the 1930 cyber helpline appears on any checked page.
